title: vLLM structured-output errors can terminate the shared EngineCore
summary: Structured-output exceptions can escape request-level error handling in three paths: the default auto backend, guidance with ngram_gpu speculative decoding, and the opt-in Rust frontend. A request triggering one of these paths can terminate the shared EngineCore and affect other tenants. The advisory groups the three paths as one request-boundary root cause and one finding.
ai_role: The vLLM project advisory explicitly states that this vulnerability was discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber as part of the Patch the Planet security initiative. This establishes AI-enabled discovery attribution; the source does not establish model autonomy or the private discovery date.
classification_note: The advisory establishes public disclosure and the documented fix scope. It does not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: The advisory describes affected versions below 0.30.0 and links proposed fix PR #51450; verify exact patched release before distribution-specific use.

impacts.conditions: Requires the corresponding structured-output backend/configuration and malformed or failure-inducing request: site 1 uses default auto backend; site 2 uses guidance plus ngram_gpu; site 3 uses the opt-in Rust frontend and an empty constraint. API-key middleware narrows site 3 to authenticated callers.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes reproducible conditions but does not report observed exploitation.
